title: Building words with prefixes and suffixes

steps.say: A prefix goes at the start of a word and changes its meaning. A suffix goes at the end.
steps.show: un + kind = unkind     kind + ness = kindness

steps.say: Some prefixes mean not. The right one often matches the first letter of the root word.
When a suffix starts with a vowel, a final e is usually dropped.
steps.show: hope + ing = hoping     fame + ous = famous

steps.say: When a suffix starts with a consonant, the e usually stays.
steps.show: hope + ful = hopeful     excite + ment = excitement

steps.say: Some endings sound alike but are spelt differently. Learn each word family.

options.why: Polite starts with p, so it takes im-, not un-.
Words starting with p take im-, not in-.

hints: Look at the first letter of polite.
Words starting with p usually take the same prefix as possible.
Say each word aloud. Which one have you heard before?
check.explanation: Polite starts with p, so its opposite takes im-: impolite.

check.prompt: Add -ing to smile. Write the new word.
hints: Look at the last letter of smile.
-ing starts with a vowel, so think about what happens to a final e.
Write smile without its last letter, then add -ing.
check.explanation: Smile ends in e and -ing starts with a vowel, so the e is dropped: smiling.
